born April 29, 1987),{{cite web|title=CA Birth Index |url=http://www.familytreelegends.com/records/calbirths?c=search&first=jeffrey&last=orcutt&spelling=Exact&4_year=1987&4_month=0&4_day=0&5=&7=&SubmitSearch.x=0&SubmitSearch.y=0 |work=FamilyTreeLegends.com |access-date=January 5, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230235758/http://www.familytreelegends.com/records/calbirths?c=search&first=jeffrey&last=orcutt&spelling=Exact&4_year=1987&4_month=0&4_day=0&5=&7=&SubmitSearch.x=0&SubmitSearch.y=0 |archive-date=December 30, 2013 }} formerly known as '''Jeff Pendergraph''', is an American professional [[basketball]] player for Indomables de Ciudad Juárez of the Liga de Básquetbol Estatal de Chihuahua. He attended [[Etiwanda High School]] in [[Rancho Cucamonga, California]] and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]].{{cite web|title=Jeff Pendergraph Arizona State bio |url=http://thesundevils.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/pendergraph_jeff00.html |work=TheSunDevils.CSTV.com |access-date=January 5, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110816070637/http://thesundevils.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/pendergraph_jeff00.html |archive-date=August 16, 2011 }} ==College career== Ayres attended Arizona State for four seasons, finishing with career averages of 12.6 points, 7.5 rebounds, 1.04 blocked shots and a 58.0 percent shooting accuracy.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Jeff Pendergraph|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail_blazers_sign_jeff_pender_2009_09_08.html|work=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2009|access-date=September 8, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090912081912/http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail_blazers_sign_jeff_pender_2009_09_08.html|archive-date=September 12, 2009|url-status=dead}} In his sophomore season, he grabbed a career-high 19 rebounds in a 52–36 victory over [[Colgate University|Colgate]] on December 19, 2006.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=263530009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105215414/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=263530009|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 5, 2012|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 4, 2009|date=December 19, 2006|title=Arizona State 52, Colgate 36}} As a senior, Ayres averaged 14.5 points and was named to the Pac-10's First Team. His 66.0 percent field goal mark led the nation. On January 4, 2009, he scored a career-high 31 points, along with a game-high 11 rebounds, in a 90–60 win over [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] with twenty-one of those points being tallied in the first half.{{cite web|url=https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290020024|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120714070437/https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290020024|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 14, 2012|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 4, 2009|date=January 4, 2009|title=Pendergraph scores career-best 31 for Sun Devils}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers=== On June 25, 2009, Ayres was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the 31st overall pick of the [[2009 NBA draft]], only to be traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Sergio Rodríguez]], the draft rights to [[Jon Brockman]] and cash considerations. On September 8, he signed a contract with the Trail Blazers and joined them for the 2009 Summer League, starting all five games and averaging 10.8 points, 7.6 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 1.2 blocked shots. On December 22, he made his NBA debut in an 85–81 win against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], in which he scored 2 points in 4 minutes of playing time.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291222006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091226201635/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291222006|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 26, 2009|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 24, 2016|date=December 23, 2009|title=Trail Blazers rally behind Roy, Aldridge to overcome Mavs in Dirk's return}} Ayres scored a career-high 23 points in the last regular season game of the [[2009–10 NBA season]] on April 14, 2010, against the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300414022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100418055750/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300414022|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 18, 2010|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 15, 2010|date=April 15, 2010|title=Curry scores 42 to lead Warriors past Blazers}} He was waived by the Trail Blazers prior to the start of the 2011 season after suffering a season-ending knee injury during a pre-season game against the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite press release|url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/1990/Default.aspx |title=Trail Blazers waive Jeff Pendergraph |publisher=Portland Trail Blazers |date=October 25, 2010 |access-date=October 25, 2010 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714204012/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/1990/Default.aspx |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }} ===Indiana Pacers=== Ayres was signed by the [[Indiana Pacers]] for the 2011–12 season. Before the start of the season, he was sidelined with a mild sprain in his knee, suffered when he injured it during a December 10, 2011, practice.{{cite web|url=http://www.indystar.com/article/20111218/SPORTS04/112180358/Pendergraph-tweaks-knee-sidelined-him-all-last-season?odyssey=tab |title=Pendergraph 'tweaks' knee that sidelined him all of last season |publisher=IndianaStar.com |date=December 18, 2011 |access-date=December 22, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526233911/http://www.indystar.com/article/20111218/SPORTS04/112180358/Pendergraph-tweaks-knee-sidelined-him-all-last-season?odyssey=tab |archive-date=May 26, 2015 }} On April 23, 2012, Ayres got his first start for the Pacers in a 103–97 win against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. In 18 minutes of play he scored 10 points with 7 rebounds, 1 assist and 2 blocks.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320423011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425054217/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320423011|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 25, 2012|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 24, 2016|date=April 24, 2012|title=Pacers slip past Pistons thanks to Paul George's 12-point 4th quarter}} On June 4, 2013, Ayres was ejected from Game 7 of the 2013 Eastern Conference Finals by referee [[Ken Mauer]] after a shoving match with [[Miami Heat]] guard [[Norris Cole (basketball)|Norris Cole]], who was also ejected in the fourth quarter.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/point-forward/2013/06/04/jeff-pendergraph-norris-cole-ejected-game-7-miami-heat-indiana-pacers|title=Norris Cole, Jeff Pendergraph, Flo Rida's manager ejected from Game 7|date=June 4, 2013|work=SI.com|access-date=June 4, 2013}} Entertainer [[Flo Rida]]'s manager was also ejected after an ongoing verbal spat with Ayres. ===San Antonio Spurs=== On July 11, 2013, Ayres signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/130711_spurs_sign_jeff_pendergraph|title=Spurs Sign Jeff Pendergraph|date=July 11, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 11, 2013}} and made his debut on October 30 in a 101–94 win against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], recording two points, two rebounds, two assists and one block in 11 minutes of playing time.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20131030/MEMSAS/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 24, 2016|date=October 30, 2013|title=Notebook: Spurs 101, Grizzlies 94}} On June 15, 2014, Ayres won his first NBA championship after the Spurs defeated the [[Miami Heat]] 4 games to 1 in the [[2014 NBA Finals]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140615/MIASAS/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 24, 2016|date=June 16, 2014|title=Notebook: Spurs 104, Heat 87|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714204113/http://www.nba.com/games/20140615/MIASAS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=July 14, 2014|url-status=dead}} ===NBA D-League and Los Angeles Clippers=== On October 31, 2015, Ayres was selected by the [[Idaho Stampede]] with the first overall pick in the [[2015 NBA Development League Draft]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-nba-d-league-draft-board/|title=2015 NBA D-League Draft Board|date=October 31, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 31, 2015|archive-date=October 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022072934/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-nba-d-league-draft-board/|url-status=dead}} On November 13, he made his debut with Idaho in a 110–106 loss to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], recording 18 points, 9 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 block and one steal in 39 minutes of action.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151113/IDARGV/|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 24, 2016|date=November 13, 2015|title=Walker Blocks Six Shots, McDaniels Scores 16 in Vipers' 110–106 Home Opener Win}} On January 29, 2016, he was named in the West All-Star team for the 2016 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|title=Sixteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2016|access-date=January 29, 2016|archive-date=February 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207115139/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|url-status=dead}} On January 23, 2016, Ayres signed a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-sign-jeff-ayres-10-day-contract|title=L.A. CLIPPERS SIGN JEFF AYRES TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 23, 2016|access-date=January 23, 2016}} The next day, he made his debut in a 112–94 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]], recording two points, one rebound and one assist in five minutes.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160124/LACTOR/gameinfo.html|title=Raptors down Clippers for eighth straight win, 112–94|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 24, 2016|access-date=January 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125215834/http://www.nba.com/games/20160124/LACTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 25, 2016|url-status=dead}} On February 2, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Clippers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-jeff-ayres-second-10-day-contract|title=L.A. CLIPPERS SIGN JEFF AYRES TO SECOND 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 2, 2016|access-date=February 2, 2016}} On February 12, the Clippers did not renew his contract, making him a free agent. On February 20, Ayres returned to Idaho, appearing on the team bench that night.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160220/RGVIDA/|title=Stampede Drive Past Vipers|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2016|access-date=February 21, 2016}} On March 4, 2016, Idaho traded Ayres to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] in exchange for a 2016 first-round draft pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/d-fenders-acquire-jeff-ayres/n-5107228|title=D-Fenders Acquire Jeff Ayres|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 4, 2016|access-date=March 4, 2016}} The next day, he made his debut for the D-Fenders in a 127–117 win over the [[Texas Legends]], recording 16 points and 10 rebounds in 26 minutes off the bench.{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160305/TEXLAD/|title=Blue Leads D-Fenders To 14th Straight Home Win|work=NBA.com|date=March 5, 2016|access-date=March 6, 2016|archive-date=March 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306221837/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160305/TEXLAD/|url-status=dead}} At the season's end, he was named to the [[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League First Team]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|title=NBA Development League Announces 2015–16 All-NBA D-League Teams|work=NBA.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904054918/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|url-status=dead}} On March 16, 2016, Ayres returned to the Clippers, signing with the team for the rest of the season.{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/l..-clippers-sign-jeff-ayres-remainder-season|title=L.A. CLIPPERS SIGN JEFF AYRES FOR REMAINDER OF SEASON|work=NBA.com|date=March 16, 2016|access-date=March 16, 2016}} ===CSKA Moscow and NBA D-League=== On September 22, 2016, Ayres signed a two-month contract with Russian club [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].{{cite web|title=CSKA added NBA champion|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=15537&lang=en|website=cskabasket.com|access-date=September 22, 2016|date=September 22, 2016|archive-date=September 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923052737/http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=15537&lang=en|url-status=dead}} Following the expiration of his contract, he parted ways with CSKA on November 23, 2016. In seven games, he averaged 5.4 points and 3.6 rebounds per game.{{cite news|title=Thank you, Jeff!|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=15658&lang=en|access-date=December 2, 2016|work=cskabasket.com|date=November 23, 2016|archive-date=December 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202233036/http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=15658&lang=en|url-status=dead}} On December 1, 2016, Ayres was reacquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders.{{cite news|title=D-Fenders Acquire Jeff was drafted by [[Bivouac (basketball)|Bivouac]] with the eighth overall pick of the 2022 [[Big3|BIG3]] draft.{{Cite web |date=2022-05-26 |title=2022 BIG3 Draft Recap |url=https://big3.com/news/2022-big3-draft-recap/ |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}} ==The Basketball Tournament== Jeff Ayres played for Team Challenge ALS in the [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|2018]] edition of [[The Basketball Tournament]]. In two games with Eberlein Drive, he averaged 6.5 points per game and 2.5 rebounds per game on 100 percent shooting.
